name: CAPGEMINI
description: Descrizione del ruolo e delle responsabilità presso Capgemini. Ad esempio: sviluppo di soluzioni software per clienti in vari settori, partecipazione a progetti di trasformazione digitale, utilizzo di tecnologie come Java, Spring Boot, Angular, ecc.

clients.description: This was my first project, where I joined a team developing internal web applications for a client in the media and advertising sector. The applications were used by the client's staff to manage the acquisition of television and radio advertising slots and packages by third parties; they were private business tools and were not publicly accessible. Working as a Full-stack Developer, I contributed to both the Angular 8 user interface and the Java/Spring Boot backend, using Oracle SQL for data storage and Spring Data JDBC for persistence. The services I developed were REST APIs within a microservices architecture. I also worked with Maven, Jenkins, SVN, and Postman as part of the development and delivery workflow. As it was my first assignment, I had to learn the project's technologies and processes quickly. I made rapid progress and, by January, was already able to handle my assigned tasks independently. Unfortunately, budget cuts resulting from the COVID-19 period meant that I was later moved to another project.

I worked on building an internal web application from the ground up to schedule and manage field interventions for the client's telecommunications infrastructure. The system supported maintenance and fault resolution across fibre-optic and copper-pair networks. From the beginning, I communicated directly with the client and independently delivered the front-end work assigned to me. For the first six months, my focus was exclusively on the front end, developing the application with Angular 11. When the colleague responsible for the back end left the project, I took ownership of the entire application, expanding my work to include its Java 8/11 and Spring Boot backend as well as its ongoing maintenance. The backend services were developed as REST APIs within a microservices architecture. Throughout the engagement, approximately every two months, I also completed a full week of 24-hour on-call availability to respond to potential issues across the client's systems, following guidance provided by the systems administrators.

Following the successful completion of my previous assignment, this client specifically requested that I rejoin their team, giving me the opportunity to build on the trust and working relationship established earlier. Although many of the systems and tools had evolved since my first engagement, I adapted quickly, drawing on my existing understanding of the team's delivery practices and ways of working. Returning as a Full-stack Developer, I contributed to the ongoing development and maintenance of the client's internal applications using Angular 13, Java 11, Spring Boot, Spring Data JDBC, and Oracle SQL. The services I developed were full REST APIs within a microservices architecture. My responsibilities grew progressively from the outset: alongside implementing assigned work, I increasingly took part in analysing requirements, breaking down tasks, and estimating the effort involved. This marked a shift from focusing primarily on delivery to taking greater ownership of the work before and during implementation.

This was my first project delivered using an Agile methodology and marked a shift toward a more collaborative, iterative front-end process. We developed web applications for managing and scheduling field work across the client's electricity networks and fibre networks of different types. The applications handled large volumes of data, so I also worked on improving performance in key workflows, particularly table data loading through pagination. The initial team consisted of a senior front-end developer and me as the middle-level developer. After receiving the client's requirements, we used Figma and the client-provided component libraries to explore and shape the user experience, then presented our proposed designs directly to the client. Once approved, we implemented the work in Angular, coordinating delivery through Jira and Git. During the final six months, as the workload increased, a junior front-end developer joined the team and I was asked to support their onboarding and training; they became productive within a few weeks. I also carried out substantial front-end refactoring, integrating microfrontends with Module Federation and upgrading the application from Angular 12 to Angular 16. In my final month, I was invited to take over the senior front-end developer's responsibilities as the client considered changing the team structure. However, contractual constraints between the client and Capgemini meant that the proposed transition could not go ahead.

I returned to back-end development, an area I particularly enjoy, contributing to the development and maintenance of an application used to remotely trigger specific operations on the client's electrical substation hardware, especially data-collection tasks. The services I developed were full REST APIs within a microservices architecture. A key part of my work was refactoring the back-end integration: the existing infrastructure relied on Apache Camel as an intermediary between incoming requests and the back-end services, and I worked on simplifying this flow by moving the relevant processing into the application. The solution was built with Java 17 and Spring Boot, with MongoDB for persistence. I also contributed to automated testing with JUnit and Mockito and used Maven, Git, Jira, and Kibana as part of the team's development and monitoring workflow.

This assignment marked my first hands-on experience with AWS and cloud services. Alongside my back-end responsibilities, I developed AWS Lambda functions in Python that were used by the client's batch processes and front-end applications, working with services including API Gateway, Secrets Manager, and CloudWatch. I also worked with MongoDB and contributed to the team's delivery and monitoring workflows using Terraform, Jenkins, Git, GitHub, Jira, Confluence, and Datadog. On the front end, I worked independently as the sole developer, taking ownership of my area and proposing and implementing new features based on the project's needs. As most of the client's planned development tasks were nearing completion, I spent the final four months helping develop a new team member who would take over my responsibilities. All Agile ceremonies were conducted in English, giving me regular experience collaborating in an English-speaking delivery process.

I joined this project to replace a senior back-end developer, taking responsibility for developing and maintaining REST APIs consumed by the client's mobile application. I independently handled the analysis, estimation, and implementation of my assigned work, contributing to a Java 17 and Spring Boot service backed by MongoDB. I also worked with JUnit, Mockito, and WireMock for testing, and with Gradle, Kubernetes, Argo, and Jenkins across the build and deployment workflow. The team followed Agile practices, with ceremonies held in English and colleagues based in Egypt. In addition to my development responsibilities, I took part in interviewing candidates to help bring new developers into the team. Unfortunately, the assignment was short-lived: a change in the client's management led to the closure of several work groups as part of a cost-reduction effort.

In this role, I develop Java-based back-end microservices and APIs consumed by the client's internal web applications, contributing to services built with Spring Boot and technologies including MongoDB and Apache Kafka. I also create Unix batch jobs that are scheduled through crontab to run at defined times, updating and integrating data received from the client's systems that record insurance claims reported by operators. One of the batch jobs I developed migrates sensitive documents from one system to another. This work combines service development with reliable data processing and integration across existing systems. I have also begun using AI-assisted development tools more regularly, including GitHub Copilot and Claude Code, to speed up task delivery while retaining responsibility for reviewing and validating the resulting code. My day-to-day workflow includes Maven, Git, Jenkins, and Argo, alongside the team's Jira and Confluence practices.
